text:
alex_g: Ran nightly perf on 8xA100 with TP=2 PP=4, FP8 quant + INT8 matmul kernels. Observed 30-40% tail latency spikes during decode for long contexts. Flame graphs point to all-reduce wait at stage boundaries. Anyone seen this?
priya_k: Can you paste the profiler output (nvprof / Nsight / NCCL timeline)?
ach alex_g: here's a short snippet from the timeline:
```
step 124: decode loop
  layer 0 forward: compute 3.8ms
  allreduce (kv sync): wait 12.3ms
  layer 1 forward: compute 4.1ms
  allreduce (kv sync): wait 11.7ms
```
Seems like allreduce wait >> compute.
cheng_w: That pattern smells like micro-batch imbalance + KV shard thrash. Are we re-syncing KV shards on every micro-batch boundary?
alex_g: Config for the job: `batch_size=8`, `micro_batch=8`, `kv_cache_enabled=true`, `kv_shard_by_layer=true`, `tp=2`, `pp=4`. We do incremental decoding with cache hits, but I see repeated NVLink traffic.
marcus_l: Micro-batch==global batch will make the pipeline steps tightly coupled. With TP=2 you can get frequent small allreduces. Also note the kernel selector recently switched to the new int8 matmul for 2048x2048 shapes — that kernel has different launch params and may interact poorly with FP8 scaling.
priya_k: We had PR #4321 that prefers the int8 kernel for certain shapes. Could be a regression in kernel selection heuristics. @cheng_w any ideas about FP8 scaling interplay with TP sharding?
cheng_w: I rolled that selector out. There's a subtlety: FP8 scale is computed per-tensor, but when KV is sharded across TP ranks the scale accumulation differs. I see scale drift: occasionally scale factor ~2.0 which can push values to FP8 saturation and cause extra corrective ops (and extra comm).
alex_g: Is there a temporary knob we can flip on Dedicated to mitigate while we debug? We need to avoid a customer-facing perf cliff.
cheng_w: Two quick mitigations: set env `REDWOOD_QUANT_FP8_SCALE_MODE=layerwise_fix` to use a stable scale calculation; and `REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=int8_fallback` to force the older int8 path. Both are non-invasive. Patch for the selector fix is in progress.
infra-bot: scheduled deploy r-2026.03.18-alpha with kernel-override env queued to staging.
priya_k: Test plan: repro job with synthetic data, long context ~16k tokens, run with and without the overrides, collect p50/p95/p99 and NCCL timelines; add microbench harness to sweep micro_batch values. I'll land a reproducible CI job.
marcus_l: Add these NCCL / nvprof flags in the job: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^docker0 NVPROF_DISABLE=0` and collect `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` + `nccl-tests` timeline. Example run command: 
```
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO nvprof --metrics all --trace-children ./run_decode.sh --config cfg.yaml
```
alex_g: Quick numbers from a dev run: baseline (no override) p95=230ms, p99=420ms; with `int8_fallback` + `layerwise_fix` p95=160ms, p99=200ms. Allreduce times reduced from ~12ms to ~3-4ms on the critical path.
cheng_w: Good signal. I'll push a hotfix to the kernel selector: validate kernel choice considering TP shards and FP8 scale variance. Also adding unit that simulates TP partitioning of scales to catch drift.
priya_k: Can we wire a regression alert in Console that watches per-model p99 post-rollout and fires if >20% increase? That would catch future rollouts faster.
alex_g: Yes please. Also add a short note in the changelog: "fix: prevent FP8 scaling overflow with TP+KV sharded decode; add kernel selection guard".
cheng_w: on it. Will follow up with PR link once CI passes. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: perf job queued: `tp-fp8-regression-check` — will post results to thread when done. :eyes:
alex_g: Thanks all — keeping this thread pinned until hotfix lands.
